title: [Refactor][Ops] Replace custom quantized Lightning Indexer with CANN native operator
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Replace the plugin-owned quantized Lightning Indexer (QLI) with the CANN operator exposed by `torch_npu.npu_quant_lightning_indexer`, removing the duplicate kernel implementation and its build and Torch registration paths.

- Switch the base device adaptor's QLI path to the native operator. Pass `INT64_MAX` for `pre_tokens` and `next_tokens` in both the base and A5 paths; A5 already used the native operator.
- Remove `csrc/attention/lightning_indexer_quant`, its build entries, and the `_C_ascend.npu_lightning_indexer_quant` binding and meta implementation.
- Update the SFA unit test to check the native call and token-window arguments, and migrate the fused quantized Lightning Indexer management test's reference call.
- Keep the custom MoeGatingTopK implementation, build entries, bindings, device adaptor behavior, and tests identical to the PR base.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

The QLI path now uses the CANN operator through `torch_npu`. The device adaptor interface is unchanged. Direct callers of the removed private `torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_lightning_indexer_quant` schema must migrate to `torch_npu.npu_quant_lightning_indexer`.

### How was this patch tested?

Validation after restoring MoeGatingTopK (October 12), against vLLM `8cc9aa5ad350f6f80cf3bebb298d410803ff75a9`:

- Device adaptor and SFA unit tests: **132 passed**.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks: passed for the five relevant Python files.
- `git diff --check b59bfc57c...HEAD`: passed.
- Confirmed the restored MoE kernel directory and tests match the PR base byte-for-byte, and all device adaptor MoE gating methods match the base.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but interrupted while installing the actionlint environment; the complete hook suite has not passed locally.
- NPU integration tests and the extension build were not rerun for this scope reduction.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pr16731-qli-vllm-verified python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/device/test_device_op.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_v1.py --maxfail=1
# 132 passed
```

Historical QLI validation (recorded before the September 23 rebase, not rerun for this scope reduction): the extension build and DeepSeek-V3.2-W8A8 TP16 inference with LI C8 enabled succeeded on CANN 9.2.0-beta.2, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, and Ascend 910B4-1.

### QLI kernel performance comparison

Historical eager-mode profiling on CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 and Ascend 910B4-1 used isolated old/native processes, 50 warmups, and 20 profiler samples per case. Across 19 eligible QLI cases, the old/native median kernel durations were `24.98 us / 22.87 us`. Representative results were `19.99 us / 15.38 us` at the 128-token block boundary and `42.94 us / 41.70 us` for the long sparse case. Two non-64-head cases were excluded because the old kernel raised an AICore address/UB error. These are kernel-only measurements; no graph capture/replay performance claim is made.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8cc9aa5ad350f6f80cf3bebb298d410803ff75a9
